# convertRichTextToMarkdown

<link-summary>Turns styled text runs back into Markdown.</link-summary>

<web-summary>convertRichTextToMarkdown() — Turns styled text runs back into Markdown. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/slide</code> · Since: 2.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function convertRichTextToMarkdown(runs: RichTextRun[], theme: Theme = {}): string;
```

The inverse of [`convertMarkdownToRichText`](convertMarkdownToRichText.md): bold, italic and strikethrough become their markers again, a run carrying a link becomes `[text](url)`, and a run set in the theme's code font becomes a code span.

A code run carries no flag of its own — it is recognised by its font — so pass the same theme both ways and the pair round-trips. Runs are written one after another in the order given, without merging neighbours that share a style, so deeply nested formatting may come back expressed differently while reading the same.

## Parameters

| Parameter                   | Type            | Description                                                              |
| :-------------------------- | :-------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `runs`                      | `RichTextRun[]` | The runs to convert. An empty array gives an empty string.               |
| `theme` _(optional)_ `= {}` | `Theme`         | The theme the runs were styled with. Only the code font is read from it. |

## Returns

`string` — the Markdown representing the runs.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                                                               |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | no argument is passed, the value is not an array, or an element is not a run with text. |

## Examples

### Back to Markdown

```javascript
const runs = convertMarkdownToRichText("**bold** and `code`");

convertRichTextToMarkdown(runs); // => "**bold** and `code`"
```

### A link keeps its text styled

```javascript
convertRichTextToMarkdown([
  { text: "site", style: { bold: true, link: { url: "https://example.com" } } }
]); // => "[**site**](https://example.com)"
```
